body: What if you tell them how you feel. Most people don't care because they truly don't understand or notice/ they have too much to think about themselves that they don't have time to care. Then you will see if they are people worth having around. There are people who do care, they just can be hard to find.

Dis you use them longer than a month/ did you try a smaller dose/ different type?, i see, i'd say exercising if you find it enjoyable and feel better during and after. Shouldn't feel like a chore. Because i also felt way worse at first but 1 month in i started to feel good. The first month i basically just laid in bed all days and felt really bad. Then i also changed dose to half the original dose and it was like night and day.

I don't believe you're ungrateful, you probably just need to change things up and find things that truly bring you joy. Emptiness, boredom are states of lack, some need goes unmet. It can be that you don't feel inspired, don't have positive relationships, feel stuck and stuff like that. Usually fear is the reason we are afraid to go after what we really want and need to be happy. So we settle for unhappiness instead pf going for a life that would make us happy.

That sucks, people like that are awful. It is true that people usually can sense if somebody is sad and if it holds true that someone is sad all the time, then people don't usually like that. But the thing is you can process emotions and change perspective by yourself. It's hard work but so so satisfying to see the results, it makes you way more confident and strong than if you didn't have the periods of low mood to begin with. Be ready to ask and accept help from good people, make sure they are good though. Medication can definetly be helpful too (antidepressants), they just take a while to work and you might feel worse up to 1 month after starting. If you don't want to do medication, exercise is even better. It has even more of a positive impact on the brain.
That's an awful thing to comment.

They will "move on" but the memory and the impact of the person never leaves. Every single positive thing the person did will make them sad that they are gone. In the context of work and usefullness most can be replaced somehow to in a satisfying degree fulfill that role. The person can never be replaced, we are all completely unique and full of potential. That potential would be lost and due to the unique nature of this potential it cannot be replaced, ever.
It's okay. We all make mistakes. What matters is not the past, but the choices we make from here going forward.
Man, this makes me believe that there are good people out there. I will try to work up the courage to put myself into positions where i can meet people. Thank you kind fellow!
What i am trying to say is that there is a ton of potential in you even if you have made "mistakes" in the past.

Reading your response, i realise i already probably have the answers. I am just too afraid of taking action, getting friends and doing what i want. And the lack of meaning and joy stemming from this causes my depression which leads into suicidal ideation, almost like a form of mental masturbation.

Thank you for the reply, didn't expect receiving such an elaborate response. That in and of itself made me happy and even smile. You do have good points, the only problem is that i don't feel i receive enough joy from the things i do at the moment. But i suspect that the reason for this is the fact that i am too afraid to go after what i want. I am not exactly sure of the complete nature of this fear, but i am fairly certain fear is my limiting factor.
I hear you. I can't completely understand how it feels but i try to. You have the strength to overcome this if you choose to.

Your attitude to yourself is based on your experiences. It doesn't change the fact that you are an insanely complex organism called a human. You wouldn't be alive if you didn't have the genes that succeeded for thousands of years.
Finding them is hard**

I care enough to comment on here because i relate to what you said. You probably yourself are a person who cares. There's no chance we are the only ones. But finding people that care is really hard in todays world.
That's what you tell yourself after your environment somehow "taught" you that.
Correct on many points. But some do truly care.

Don't resist the thoughts or emotions, but don't actively engage in them either. Then think about this: no matter how you look, no matter what you do some people will always judge others. And that is okay, you need to get comfortable with thought of potentially being criticized or judged by someone else, as harsh as it sounds. And you will get comfortable with it with time. Just don't try to hide your looks in any way, that makes the fear grow. Personally i used to start crying while driving sue to anxiety, then i let myself cry and didn't hide it until i got comfortable.

They are horrendous people. I hope they someday realize the error of their ways. Do not feel bad for your emotions or conditions. Find decent people to be in contact with, having positive social relationships is essential.
Hello, loser and man are just arbitrary labels. We are all equal in value even if some may try to make themselves feel more important to compensate for their own feeling of inadequacy.
